# r1-iter-b notes

## What I built (proposal.json, generated by scripts/build.py)
All recognition happens in the encoder; it emits a 12x13 logit table and the step
bundle just selects row `step` (one-hot from coords vs step, matmul). state_dim stays 0.
- `align` bundle: rowmax > 0.5 -> first ink row (via `first_on`: step, cumsum, step(1.5-cs))
  -> one-hot times a constant shift basis Pv[32,15*32] gives a 15-row crop starting at the
  glyph top. Colmax > 0.5 -> first ink column (searched in cols 0..23) -> shift basis
  Ph[24,128*104] aligns so leftmost ink sits at column 4.
- `reader` bundle: 4 candidate left bearings (shift 0..3), each via shared `read_cells`
  (slice 96 cols -> 8 cells of 15x12 -> `cell_templates` cell). Picks the bearing whose
  best class score on cell 0 is highest (onehot_argmax) and uses it for all 8 cells.
- `cell_templates` cell: 10 hand-typed 15x12 ascii glyph templates (# and + -> +1,
  : and . -> 0, blank -> -1) with bias 0.5*(N_bg - N_ink), i.e. score = sum_ink(x-0.5) +
  sum_bg(0.5-x); 11th row = ink sum over cell cols 2..9 (presence).
- `to_table`: digit logits + 1000*step(presence-4); EOS column fixed 500; pad/bos -1e4;
  rows 8..11 padded with 0 so they always emit EOS.

## Key numbers and why (chosen by viewing dev PNGs as ascii dumps)
- Pitch 12 px (DejaVu Sans Mono at 20 px), glyphs 15 rows tall with top = 8 + y_jitter,
  ink starts at origin+1 or +2 -> bearing candidates 0..3 relative to first ink.
- Thresholds 0.5 are far above noise (sigma <= 0.03) and below stroke intensity.

## Observed (dev_main, n=400)
- evals/000: exact 1.000, CER 0.000, all lengths 1-8 correct, 0 failures.
- evals/001 (same proposal, --trace rd; trace covers 24 cases): top1-top2 template gap
  min 11.5 / median 21.8 on 114 present cells; presence min 40.9 (present) vs max 1.6
  (absent); chosen bearing offsets: 1 (20 cases), 2 (4 cases).
- Dev-evals used: 2 of 25.

## Hypotheses / risks / next
- Relies on fixed font size, pitch 12, and integer x; a different size or proportional
  font would break templates and the cell grid (hypothesis, untested).
- Heavy blur or stronger noise could shift the first-ink column; the bearing search
  (0..3) gives some slack. Ph dominates param storage (~319k floats); a shift-and-sum
  over 24 fixed `op:shift` copies would be cheaper in params but more nodes.
